_doc: Expected tool trajectories for the 10 Week-7 questions, asserted by eval/week8/trajectory_eval.py.
Each case lists EVERY acceptable core path as {core, h_min}. A run matches a path when its
non-H calls equal `core` in order and it made at least `h_min` handbook searches.
search_handbook POSITION is never asserted: reading the handbook before or after the
jurisdiction rule are both correct, and asserting one order would score correct runs as
failures. Extra H calls are tolerated by the matcher too (H is read-only over one corpus);
they are charged to step efficiency instead. Any unexpected R or J call fails the match.
steps_needed = min over paths of len(core) + h_min.

q01.alt: 2 paths. The 2-week figure exists only in HB-08-1, so H is required; checking the US-NY override first (it defers to the handbook) is a legitimate detour, not a wrong path.

q02.alt: 2 paths. The 10-week figure exists only in the handbook addendum (HB-10-1), so H is required; the US-CA parental rule only says 'company-wide applies', reading it is legitimate.

q03.alt: 2 paths. The 5-day carry-over cap is stated in BOTH HB-01-2 and the US-NY rule, so record+handbook and record+rule are each sufficient (mirrors the q03 any-of citation in the outcome eval).

q04.alt: 1 path. Statutory notice by tenure lives only in the UK rule; the record must be read first (jurisdiction AND tenure band come from it). H optional.

q05.alt: 1 path. Same as q04, different tenure band - the record read is what proves the 9-week answer wasn't a guess.

q06.alt: 1 path. DE probation band: the record's 2 months of service is the branching fact.

q07.alt: 1 path. The US-CA no-forfeiture rule decides it; the record supplies the PTO balance.

q08.alt: 2 paths. The prior record and the UK rule can be fetched in either order; R:E1012 must come first (E0877 is only discoverable from it). A run that never fetches E0877 cannot know the 8 years.

q09.alt: 2 paths. Both jurisdictions' PTO figures are needed for the pro-rating; either order after the record. A run with only J:DE is the 24-day wrong answer's wrong path.

q10.alt: 2 paths. Like q08: prior record E0655 and the DE rule in either order after R:E1015.
